The '''Pacithhip''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Shimia/Legends|Shimia]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Members of the species were short, squat [[pachydermoid]] bipeds with long, thick tails and rough, [[Color/Legends|blue]], green or gray skin. To fit in with a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]]-dominated [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], Pacithhip often employed [[robotic stilts]] to achieve greater height and to use technology crafted for standard humanoids. The Pacithhip face featured a long trunk, four nostrils, and two elaborate tusks. The tusks came in three distinct patterns, which determined whether their bearer was a member of the scholar, [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]], or [[Farm/Legends|farmer]] caste. Most Pacithhip made peace with their genetically determined place in society, but a few rejected the system and sought their fortune offworld. Pacithhip were broad-minded and adaptable to foreign environments.

The Pacithhip were discovered before [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], in the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade route]] eventually reached Shimia, and the Pacithhip gained access to galactic-standard technology. Pacithhip colonists reached faraway planets; for example, by [[35 BBY/Legends|35 BBY]], [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] boasted a significant Pacithhip population, many of whom were animal breeders. After the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Imperial [[Troop/Legends|troops]] took over Shimia's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and discouraged offworld travel but otherwise left the Pacithhip alone. The Imperial defeat at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] freed the Pacithhip to once again spread throughout the galaxy.

Since their discovery by the Galactic Republic, Pacithhip integrated into the galaxy. One such individual was a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who fought in the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] during the [[New Sith Wars]]. [[Durundo]] was a [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] active during the latter days of the Republic. [[Ketwol/Legends|Ketwol]] was a Pacithhip prospector who settled on Tatooine and frequented [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Pacithhip_mother_and_child.png|thumb|left|200px|A Pacithhip mother and child view a [[Bursa/Legends|bursa]] on Coruscant.]]
Pacithhip were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]]<ref name="AE " /> [[pachydermoid]]s who walked upright on stubby [[Limb/Legends|legs]]. Coupled with a long tail, this gave them a low center of [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] and made them surefooted and stable<ref name="UAA" /> Nevertheless, these short limbs made them slower than most [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and prevented them from operating standard machinery and vehicles. Many Pacithhip wore [[robotic stilts]] that raised their height from their natural 1.3 to 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> and gave them the proportions of an average humanoid,<ref name="CSWE III 4">{{CSWECite|III|4|Pacithhip}}</ref> although this behavior was far from universal.<ref name="Bad Business">{{Tales|8|Bad Business}}</ref> Because Pacithhip young often hitched rides on their elders' backs, their speed was not as much of a disadvantage.<ref name="WLOSW">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref><ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> The Pacithhip had hairless, wrinkled skin that ranged in [[Color/Legends|color]]'' from blue<ref name="AF " /> to green to gray.<ref name="UAA" /> It was thick and tough,<ref name="NEGAS" /> which afforded them some resistance to physical damage<ref name="UAA" /> and [[Stun/Legends|stun]] [[Laser/Legends|blasts]].<ref name="JFF">''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]''</ref> The hands of some Pacithhip had three short, stubby fingers,<ref name="AE " /> while others sported four long and thin digits.<ref name="WLOSW" /> Pacithhip adjusted easily to environmental extremes.<ref name="UAA" />

A thick ridge of [[Bone/Legends|bone]] at the back of the skull protected the Pacithhip head. Above this and high on the sides of the head were two large [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that gave the Pacithhip a full 360-degree field of vision.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Their eyes came in different hues, but blue was particularly common.<ref name="eyes" /> A long proboscis jutted from the front of the face and ended in two nostrils; Pacithhip could drink through the trunk and even squirt jets of liquid from it.<ref name="JVS3">[[Jedi vs. Sith 3|''Jedi vs. Sith'' 3]]</ref> This trunk was flanked by two larger nostrils at its base.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The large mouth opened widely.<ref name="AOTC comic 1">[[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones 1|''Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones'' 1]]</ref> Many Pacithhip had deep, gravelly voices.<ref name="TPMG">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

The species' most distinctive feature was a pair of elaborate tusks that grew from the base of the skull ridge and stuck out to either side of the nose<ref name="AE " />&mdash;although at least some Pacithhip had no tusks at all.<ref name="AF " /> These were covered in skin for much of their length,<ref name="WLOSW" /> but these fleshy growths terminated in tufts of black [[Hair/Legends|fur]] in some specimens.<ref name="CoE3" /> The final third resembled ivory-colored bone or [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], jutting up at an angle in some individuals,<ref name="WLOSW" /> growing out straight in others.<ref name="EIVD ">[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary'']]</ref> The tusks were deadly in combat but served primarily to aid in depth perception.<ref name="AE " /> They came in three genetically determined patterns.<ref name="UAA" /> Some Pacithhip adorned them with [[Ring/Legends|rings]] and bands.<ref name="Malastare">[[Star Wars (1998) 15|''Star Wars'' (1998) 15]]</ref> Young Pacithhip had undifferentiated tusks until the onset of adolescence at thirteen [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard years]] of age, with the full tusk pattern emerging by adulthood, at eighteen standard years.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Pacithhip life expectancy was eighty-five standard years.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Ketwol-ANH.png|thumb|right|300px|The shape of a Pacithhip's tusks determined his or her caste.]]
[[Shimia/Legends|Shimia's]] 10 to 100 million Pacithhip<ref name="EA ">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> were divided into three castes: scholars, [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], and [[Farm/Legends|farmers]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> Pacithhip viewed the castes as equal in rights and duties with no caste-based discrimination, but each had predetermined tasks they were expected to execute.<ref name="AE " /> The scholars acted as legal experts, [[Judge/Legends|judges]], [[Administrator/Legends|administrators]], and teachers. The warriors upheld the mandates of the scholars and provided Pacithhip communities with defense. The farmers were the most diverse; although originally responsible for food production and textile work, in later years they took on manufacturing tasks on a greater scale. Membership in a particular caste was determined by the shape of a Pacithhip's tusks.<ref name="NEGAS" /> This could be determined early in a Pacithhip's life through genetic testing,<ref name="CSWE III 4" /> but the tusks of a few Pacithhip failed to differentiate, making their place in society liminal.<ref name="Askol CCG">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=Bok Askol}}</ref>

The Pacithhip were logical and broad-minded beings. Their society condoned and encouraged stoicism; their preferred approach to dealing with the disagreeable&mdash;even something as fundamental as dislike of the caste system&mdash;was to let it be and endure. They believed it best to follow authority, especially the scholar caste. These intellectuals emphasized egalitarianism and equality, so Pacithhip were unafraid of, even intrigued by, other species. Therefore, they easily adjusted to different cultures and conditions.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The language of the Pacithhip was known as [[Shimiese/Legends|Shimiese]], a tongue that combined proboscis toots, dense oral vocalizations, and quick nasal huffs.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Written Shimiese employed pictograms that stood for idioms and various parts of speech.<ref name="UAA" /> Pacithhip could easily understand and speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> At least those Pacithhip who lived among members of other species used gestures standard for much of galactic society, such as shaking their head to indicate ''no''.<ref name="BHP 7">''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 2: Curse of the Black Hole Pirates]]''</ref>

[[File:Pacithhip_jerba_breeder.png|thumb|left|250px|A Pacithhip breeder from Tatooine shows jerbas on Coruscant.]]
After their discovery by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and integration to the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|trade route]], the Pacithhip gained access to advanced technology and [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]]. Nevertheless, their native manufacturing and [[Engineer/Legends|engineering]] capabilities lagged behind those of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large for most of their history; by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], they were still in their industrial period.<ref name="AE " /> Nevertheless, offworld Pacithhip could become quite adept at analyzing [[Starship/Legends|starship]] malfunctions, even if they had to be careful not to tangle their tusks in the complex wiring of [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] and other equipment.<ref name="BHP 7" /> The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] presence on Shimia did its best to slow the Pacithhip's technological progress, but with the rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the species was once again able to engage in trade with the galaxy on a large scale.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
[[File:Pacithhip-JvS.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Pacithhip Jedi served in the Army of Light, in 1,000 BBY.]]
The Pacithhip evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Shimia,<ref name="NEGAS" /> in the [[Dalchon sector/Legends|Dalchon sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> The world was dominated by temperate [[Grass/Legends|grassland]] that abutted coastal mountain ranges.<ref name="UAA" /> The Pacithhip evolved from creatures with tough, lengthy tusks used for defense and sexual competition. As the beings grew more intelligent, these features became smaller and more refined.<ref name="AE " />

Shimia was first reached by outsiders between [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000]] and [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], during the Galactic Republic's settlement of the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] in which the world was located. The remote world lay just south of the Corellian Run trade route,<ref name="EA " /> and over time, commercial Republic interests built several spaceports on the world.<ref name="AE " /> The planet fell within territory considered both [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] and part of the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] during the [[New Sith Wars]] of [[1004 BBY|1004]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. Years later, the Pacithhip's planet was in unaligned [[Realspace/Legends|space]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="EA " /> During the conflict, the Republic suspected that a gang of Pacithhip [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] led by the Pacithhip [[Kozzel Qwok]] were having dealings with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and so spent several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] trying to find the criminals.<ref name="Crisis on Coruscant">''[[The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny: Crisis on Coruscant]]''</ref>

Over millennia of contact with offworlders, the Pacithhip imported and embraced galactic technology. Their own manufacturing capabilities, however, remained primitive; they had only approached the industrial level&mdash;fossil [[Fuel/Legends|fuels]] and precision machinery<ref name="UAA" />&mdash;by the time of the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="AE " />

This relative backwardness and reliance on imported technology helped the Galactic Empire conquer the world after the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="UAA" /> The new government contented itself with taking over operations of Shimia's spaceports, monitoring traffic to and from the planet, and discouraging Pacithhip from traveling offworld; otherwise, it left the Pacithhip to their own devices.<ref name="AE " /> With the defeat of the Empire in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Pacithhip reclaimed their spaceports and pursued larger-scale trade with the outside galaxy. When the New Republic was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|established]], more and more Pacithhip ventured off Shimia.<ref name="UAA" /> In [[137 ABY]], the world fell within territory controlled by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="EA " />

==Pacithhip in the galaxy==
[[File:TallPacithhip-CVD.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Pacithhip, such as this podracer mechanic in Mos Espa, often wore robotic stilts to pass as humanoid.]]
In the centuries after their first contact with the Galactic Republic, several Pacithhip left their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] to explore the greater galaxy,<ref name="AE " /> and members of the species could be found from the Rim to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]].<ref name="CSWE III 4" /> Some of these opposed their world's rigid caste system and sought instead to make their own destinies in the galaxy. However, rather than branding these dissidents outcasts or ostracizing them from society, members of the scholar caste encouraged them to seek their own ways, especially after the fall of the Empire.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Offworld Pacithhip often took up the life of [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]], [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]], or [[Scout/Legends|scouts]].<ref name="UAA" /> Such Pacithhip were more likely to employ robotic stilts and hide their tails to better fit in with other species.<ref name="DB Ketwol">{{DB|character|ketwol|Ketwol}}</ref>

Pacithhip integrated into the greater galaxy for centuries. A Pacithhip [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] was a member of the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] in 1,000 BBY,<ref name="JVS3" /> while another Pacithhip was known to be a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] wielder.<ref name="Alien Encounters">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> By [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], a number of Pacithhip lived in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]];<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref><ref name="Episode I: Queen Amidala">''[[Episode I: Queen Amidala]]''</ref> one of their number, [[Bok Askol/Legends|Bok Askol]], served as a factotum<ref name="RG">{{InsiderCite|131|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: An Audience of Aliens}}</ref> and prospector.<ref name="Askol CCG" /> [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="EIIG">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> where they befriended other [[City/Legends|city]] dwellers; [[Anakin Skywalker's friend|one]] befriended the [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] boy [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], for example.<ref name="TPMG" /> Tatooine's Pacithhip were known as skilled animal breeders; at least a few such Pacithhip made trips to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to sell their beasts. The Tatooine [[Jerba/Legends|jerba]] was one rare breed they raised.<ref name="WLOSW" /> Pacithhip in the Republic gravitated toward [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]]. One worked as a [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] on Tatooine,<ref name="EIVD " /> [[:File:BithBand.jpg|another]] performed in a band at the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] of 32 BBY,<ref name="EIIG" /> and another, known as [[Durundo]], was a podracer who competed in the final race of the [[Vinta Harvest Classic/Legends|Vinta Harvest Classic]] on [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] in 32 BBY.<ref name="Malastare" /> Pacithhip were also present at the [[Casino District (Ord Mantell)|Casino District]] of [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]].<ref name="Rite 43">[[Star Wars (1998) 43|''Star Wars'' (1998) 43]]</ref> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> the patron [[Palee Ruda]] was accompanied by Pacithhip escort<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|75|Who's Who in the Outlander Club: It's Ladies' Night}}</ref> while exiting the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]]. Inside the club, the socialite [[Sel Maa]] talked to a Pacithhip.<ref name="aotc">{{Film|II}}</ref> Pacithhip were also present at [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] that same year.<ref name="AOTC comic 1" /> [[:File:Pacithhip circus performer.png|Another member of the species]] was part of a [[Circus/Legends|circus]] that performed on Coruscant.<ref name="WLOSW" /> A Pacithhip delegation was present in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] when [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] declared the formation of the Galactic Empire in 19 BBY.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Later, during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a stilt-wearing [[Unidentified Pacithhip pirate|Pacithhip pirate]] served as part of the [[Black Hole Gang/Legends|Black Hole Gang]], a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] who had become trapped in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] due to the [[Gravity/Legends|gravitational]] pull of a [[Unidentified black hole|black hole]]. This Pacithhip was eventually freed from this predicament when Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Nuru Kungurama]] opened a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] portal using an ancient [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] [[Star Temple]].<ref name="BHP 7" />

During the Imperial occupation of Shimia, emigration was discouraged, although it was never outlawed,<ref name="AE " /> and Pacithhip suffered from government [[High Human Culture/Legends|anti-alien policies]]. Indeed, a Pacithhip was among other job seekers at the [[Coruscant Employment Center]] in 19 BBY,<ref name="Evasive Action: Recruitment">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref> and sometime before 0 BBY,<ref name="date">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]'' takes place between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]'' and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The attraction refers to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and must therefore take place after the foundation of that group; according to ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', the Alliance was officially formed in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] with the signing of the [[Corellian Treaty]].</ref> a [[Unidentified Pacithhip passenger|Pacithhip passenger]] was featured by the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency in a safety program for passengers on the [[StarSpeeder 1000]].<ref name="ST2">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> Some members of the species chose to collaborate with the new government in exchange for bribes; Pacithhip businessbeings on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], for example, sold the Empire the names of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] financial backers on that world.<ref name="Card-CCG-Dantooine Operative">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Dantooine Operative}}</ref> [[Erkwil]] was a Pacithhip [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Drug dealer|dealer]] who lived in Mos Eisley on Tatooine.<ref name="Tosche">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20010621a2|text=A Night at Tosche Station|int=A Night at Tosche Station}}</ref> [[Ketwol/Legends|Ketwol]] was an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] [[Miner/Legends|miner]] and prospector who traveled widely during the period of the Galactic Civil War<ref name="DB Ketwol" /> selling precious metals and booking charters. Although he came off as mysterious to those who met him, Ketwol was kind to others,<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and he befriended the Tatooine street thief [[Swilla Corey]].<ref name="DB-Swilla Corey">{{DB|character|swillacorey|Corey, Swilla}}</ref> He shared a jigger of [[Merenzane Gold/Legends|Merenzane Gold]] with a [[Defel/Legends|Defel]] and a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] in the Mos Eisley [[Cantina/Legends|Cantina]] around the time [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] hired smugglers [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] for passage to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="ITWOSWT ">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Pacithhip joined the throngs on Coruscant cheering the Empire's fall.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref> With the rise of the New Republic, Pacithhip became more and more common off their homeworld, especially along the Corellian Run, where many became [[Merchant/Legends|traders]].<ref name="UAA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I object! I mean, come on! That wolf-guy wasn't even there!|Han Solo|<ref name="The Emperor's Court">{{Tales|14|The Emperor's Court}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ketwol24.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Hasbro Ketwol action figure shows the robotic stilts used by Pacithhip to appear humanoid.]]
The character Ketwol was the first Pacithhip to appear in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]. An artist at [[Industrial Light & Magic]] designed the character, and [[Howie Weed]] sculpted and painted the puppet for use in the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] release of the film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="BTM" /> Known as "the elephant," the character, puppeteered by Weed, was digitally inserted into the film's cantina scene.<ref name="Factoids">{{InsiderCite|78|50 Factoids About the Original Star Wars Trilogy|50 Factoids About the Original ''Star Wars'' Trilogy}}</ref> Ketwol replaced the [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]],<ref name="DB Ketwol" /> a character whose unarticulated mask had bothered [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Factoids" /> The Ketwol mask was reversed to become the character [[Melas/Legends|Melas]], who replaced another [[Wolf/Legends|wolf-like]] character, the Defel [[Arleil Schous/Legends|Arleil Schous]], in the same scene.<ref name="DB Ketwol" /><ref name="Ask Lobot">{{InsiderCite|71|Ask Lobot|Star Wars Q&A}}</ref> However, the [[Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition|''Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition'' comic]] keeps Sivrak in this scene,<ref name="Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition 1">[[Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition 1|''Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition'' 1]]</ref> and the non-canonical story "[[The Emperor's Court]]" in [[Star Wars Tales 14|''Star Wars Tales'' 14]] makes fun of Lucas's changes through [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] protest against Lak Sivrak's testimony damning him for the shooting of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]]; after all, as of the ''Special Edition'', Sivrak was not present in the cantina to witness Greedo's [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="The Emperor's Court" />

The appearance of the Pacithhip has varied from source to source. The [[1998]] [[West End Games]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Alien Encounters]]'' depicts a long-legged, humanoid Pacithhip with three-fingered hands.<ref name="AE " /> However, in concept art for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] included several Pacithhip among the denizens of Mos Espa&mdash;including an early concept for the [[Swokes Swokes/Legends|Swokes Swokes]] [[Gorgmonger/Legends|gorgmonger]] [[Gragra/Legends|Gragra]]&mdash;all of them as tall as a [[Human/Legends|Human]], but with decidedly non-humanoid bodies with long tails, short legs, and four long fingers.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> The production crew of the film created several Pacithhip masks for the film's extras, so several Pacithhip background characters appear in the [[Prequel trilogy|''Star Wars'' prequel trilogy]] who fit this same general build as West End's Pacithhip, not Whitlatch's.<ref name="DB Ketwol" /> The Whitlatch design resurfaced in the [[2001]] book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', which recycles some of the concept art from ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="WLOSW" /> The [[2003]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] supplement ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' follows Whitlatch's design.<ref name="UAA" /> Still other sources, such as the cover to ''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]'', show only the head and shoulders of Pacithhip characters and leave the body in doubt. To explain this discrepancy, the [[Hasbro]] Ketwol action figure was designed with mechanical stilts that could be hidden by trousers,<ref name="JFF" /> a notion that later sources, such as the "Ketwol" [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry<ref name="DB Ketwol" /> and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', support as a species quirk.<ref name="CSWE III 4" /> Sources have yet to explain why some Pacithhip have three fingers and others four.

In both the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|West End Games]] and [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|Wizards of the Coast]] ''Star Wars'' roleplaying games, Pacithhip are available for players to use as characters. Both game systems' statistics for the species make them slightly clumsy and slow-moving, though strong relative to Humans.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="AE " />
